prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor rock-climbing scene with boulders and a steep rock wall about 3 to 6 metres ahead, and three people at distinct depth layers across the five frames as the camera wearer turns right and tilts up and down. A person in a dark cap stands within arm's reach (under 1 metre, bright white) in the lower right of frame 1 and shifts to the left edge of frames 2–4 (partly out of view), while a climber in a yellow helmet stands 1.5–2.5 metres in front of the wearer and about 1–1.5 metres in front and to the left of a third climber in a white helmet (roughly 3–4 metres away, holding a vertical rope within arm's reach). None of the three people look directly at the camera wearer: the capped person looks down and right, the yellow-helmeted climber faces away toward the rock wall and turns their head slightly right in frame 5, and the white-helmeted climber faces right in profile while tilting their head from upward in frames 2–3 to downward in frames 4–5. The depth map clearly separates the foreground climbers from the similarly textured rock wall and captures the thin climbing rope in frames 2–5, which blends into the rock in RGB. However, it is unreliable on the distant climber at the far right edge of frame 1 (blending them into the dark background) and over-smooths fine harness hardware and rock crevices.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only the `person` class against a black background, tracking up to three people per frame across the five frames. In frame 1, it segments the nearby capped person in the lower right (within 1 metre) and a tiny distant person at the upper right edge (over 8 metres away), who is very hard to spot in the RGB image. In frames 2 through 5, as the camera turns right, it tracks the capped person as a partial cyan mask on the far left edge (frames 2–4), the yellow-helmeted climber in pink at 1.5–2.5 metres in the centre, and the white-helmeted climber in brown at 3–4 metres to the right. The masks clearly show spatial occlusions, particularly in frame 5 where the nearer yellow-helmeted climber steps slightly right and partially occludes the left side of the further white-helmeted climber, and in frame 4 where the yellow-helmeted climber's head is clipped at the top edge. The map is unreliable for non-human objects—completely omitting the boulders, helmets as separate items, harnesses, and climbing ropes—and leaves small false-negative gaps inside the yellow-helmeted climber's hood and back in frames 2 and 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank, detecting a single yellow body skeleton only in frame 4 for the white-helmeted climber standing roughly 3–4 metres ahead and to the right of the camera wearer. In that frame, the skeleton shows the climber standing upright on a rock ledge above the camera wearer's waist level, facing right in profile with head tilted down toward their hands, which are held at waist height within arm's reach of the climbing rope. Compared to the RGB image, the skeleton isolates the exact joint positions and rightward-facing alignment of this full-body figure without visual clutter from the rock face or climbing gear. However, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence, failing to detect any magenta hand skeletons anywhere and completely missing all other people in frames 1–5. Even on the single detected figure in frame 4, the left and right leg and arm joints are collapsed nearly on top of one another due to the side-profile viewpoint and self-occlusion.
